keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Newfoundland was an English, and later British, colony established in 1610 on the island of Newfoundland'; 'John Guy was governor of the first settlement at Cuper's Cove.' France held the rest of the island (Plaisance) until Utrecht; only the English Avalon settlements are drawn (the researcher's reading; the page gives no extent). Soft.
New keyframe. 'Under the terms of the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 France ceded all Newfoundland to Great Britain.' The gazetteer's island is about 103,000 km2.

ledger.note: 1610: the Newfoundland colony. 'Newfoundland was an English, and later British, colony established in 1610 on the island of Newfoundland'; 'John Guy was governor of the first settlement at Cuper's Cove.'

1713: France cedes Newfoundland. 'Under the terms of the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 France ceded all Newfoundland to Great Britain'; the Utrecht page has the cessions of 'Nova Scotia and its claims to Newfoundland' in the treaties of 11 April 1713.

region.text: the coastal strip of Labrador: 'At that time, Labrador was limited to a coastal strip' (the strip's width is the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1763: the Labrador coast is attached to Newfoundland. 'Labrador's dependency was created and given to the Newfoundland colony by royal proclamation' so it could administer fishing rights; 'limited to a coastal strip'. The previous holder is read as New France (the territory was ceded by France in 1763); the page does not say.

region.text: the coastal strip of Labrador: 'At that time, Labrador was limited to a coastal strip' (the strip's width is the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1774: Labrador goes to Quebec. 'The Quebec Act gave the Province of Quebec control over lands that had been assigned to Newfoundland in 1763. Newfoundland kept its authority over fishing.'

region.text: the coastal strip of Labrador: 'At that time, Labrador was limited to a coastal strip' (the strip's width is the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1809: Labrador returns to Newfoundland. 'In 1809, the British Imperial government detached Labrador from Lower Canada for transfer to the Newfoundland Colony' (Lower Canada page: 'transferred to Newfoundland in 1809').

1825: Newfoundland becomes a Crown colony. The intro says 'Newfoundland was made a Crown colony in 1824' and the body 'It became an official Crown colony in 1825'; Thomas John Cochrane was the first governor; representative government 1832, self-government 1854.

region.text: the interior of Labrador beyond the coastal strip, awarded by the 1927 decision: the frontier runs 'the crest of the watershed of the rivers flowing into the Atlantic Ocean' to Cape Chidley

ledger.note: 1902: the Labrador boundary dispute. 'A dispute arose between Quebec and Newfoundland over a timber licence on the Churchill River' and went to the Privy Council; in 1898 the Quebec Boundary Extension Act had extended Quebec's northern frontier to the Eastmain River.
1907: Newfoundland becomes a dominion on 26 September 1907 ('Semi-sovereign dominion: 26 September 1907'; the Dominion page's own statement of the Imperial Conference carries a citation-needed tag).

region.text: the interior of Labrador beyond the coastal strip, awarded by the 1927 decision: the frontier runs 'the crest of the watershed of the rivers flowing into the Atlantic Ocean' to Cape Chidley

ledger.note: 1927: the Privy Council awards the interior of Labrador to Newfoundland. On 1 March 1927 (the Dominion page: 1 April) the Judicial Committee 'sided with Newfoundland', the frontier following 'the crest of the watershed of the rivers flowing into the Atlantic Ocean' to Cape Chidley; the King approved on 22 March 1927.

ledger.note: 1927: the Labrador dispute ends with the Privy Council decision (1 March 1927); Quebec has never formally recognised it.
1934: self-government is suspended. 'On 16 February 1934, the British government appointed six commissioners' (Commission of Government).

ledger.note: 1949: Newfoundland joins Canada. 'Newfoundland joined Canada in the final hours of 31 March 1949'; referendums on 3 June and 22 July 1948. The Newfoundland Act defined the province to include the Coast of Labrador as delimited in 1927.

wars.name: Labrador boundary dispute

zones.text: the interior of Labrador beyond the coastal strip, awarded by the 1927 decision: the frontier runs 'the crest of the watershed of the rivers flowing into the Atlantic Ocean' to Cape Chidley

wars.outcome: A legal dispute, not a war: the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council sided with Newfoundland on 1 March 1927 and the King approved on 22 March 1927.
wars.note: The dispute was formally between Quebec and Newfoundland. Quebec has never officially recognised the 1927 decision (2001 statement by ministers Brassard and Facal on the page).

certainty.note: The island's coast is a natural border, but the colony's extent in the 1610 settlement and the Labrador limits (coastal strip only; the interior undefined) are approximate; the French Shore rights are not on the pages.
The Labrador boundary was fixed by the Privy Council decision of 1927 along the Atlantic watershed (Quebec disputes it).

notes: Not a Cliopatria row (the english-colonial-empire notes list Newfoundland among the possessions that row draws to 1712; british-colonial-empire draws it after). Written as one state, Colony then Dominion (rename events 1825, 1907, 1934), under the slug the Canada dossier already uses. Pages: Colony of Newfoundland, Dominion of Newfoundland, Labrador boundary dispute, Treaty of Utrecht, Lower Canada (five). Not on the pages: the French Shore (1783, 1904), St. Pierre and Miquelon, the Treaty of Paris 1763 fishing clauses, the 1763 French cession of Plaisance details, wartime bases (Argentia is not on the page). Disagreements: Crown colony 1824 (intro) vs 1825 (body); Privy Council decision 1 March 1927 (Labrador dispute page) vs 1 April 1927 (Dominion page); the capital spans are the researcher's. The province-of-quebec 1774 gain does not mention Labrador because it was written before the dispute page was opened; see its notes.
